\section[amita, amitae]{amita, amitae — an aunt (father's sister)}

\label{lesson:LA-C72-amita}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for a baby, then the Latin for an uncle.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: amita, amitae}
\textbf{amita, amitae} — \textquotedblleft{}an aunt (father's sister)\textquotedblright{}. English \emph{aunt} comes from it.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for aunt, neighbour, guest, man, woman.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{amita}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{amita}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{amita}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Latin for a baby, then the Latin for an uncle, then say \emph{amita} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does amita, amitae mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An aunt (father's sister)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
